authoritative_for: Paperboy owns version-one TOML renderer manifests, configuration validation, literal command execution, successful stdout handoff, and selection of its per-job Clockwork definitions.
Paperboy owns the halt-until-approved declaration and job schedule controls. Clockwork owns enforcement, retained incidents, activation history, and schedule delivery evidence.
not_authoritative_for: Renderers own collection, data windows, source access, side effects, content, and source accuracy. Email and Resend own fixed-recipient submission; Gmail owns final delivery. Clockwork and launchd own activation and timer delivery.

covers: All public Paperboy manifest initialization, configured-job reads, manual rendering and sending, schedule application and control, diagnostics, status observations, and maintained installation outcomes.
excludes: Help/version, internal execution handoff, source-specific adapters, agent execution, configurable recipients, retained messages, report history, retry queues, email reconciliation, and legacy report recovery.

shared_access_and_trust: Current-user local interfaces. Renderer commands are trusted normal-user programs with no Paperboy sandbox. Arguments are literal; the renderer receives only HOME, a fixed PATH, and CHANCERY_USAGE_INTERNAL=1. Runtime does not invoke Chancery discovery.
shared_privacy_and_retention: Manifests, definition metadata, paths, arguments, subjects, and logs are private local data. Paperboy retains no rendered body or structured send ledger. Logs can retain result metadata, including accepted provider message IDs, and bounded script stderr. Clockwork retains activation metadata, not renderer output.
Email discloses successful nonempty stdout and its selected subject to Resend and Gmail. Credentials remain with Email and the script configuration authority.

CLI usage recording requires nonempty CODEX_THREAD_ID. The private journal records command identity, time, and thread ID, not arguments, output, or outcomes. Internal product calls are excluded and recording errors preserve results.
compatibility_and_retirement: Paperboy 0.3.0 and report contract five replace the legacy report interface. TOML manifest version one is separate from product and Clockwork schemas. The retired SQLite database remains unopened and unchanged; new runtime exposes no legacy recovery operations.
operational_limits: Renderer execution is bounded to 1200 seconds, stdout to 64000 UTF-8 bytes, stderr diagnostics to 4096 bytes, Email observation to 120 seconds, and Clockwork activation to 1380 seconds. Different jobs can run concurrently; one scheduled binding skips overlap. No trigger-delay or inbox-delivery objective is promised.
